canada.title: Out of sight: School division bans smart glasses
canada.summary: A Manitoba school division has issued an outright ban on smart glasses in response to multiple instances of students showing up to class in wearable technology that can make discreet recordings.

canada.title: Ice rink users in Nanaimo, B.C., call for construction of new arena
canada.summary: Nanaimo, B.C., ice rink users say the best time to build a new arena was 10 years ago, but the second best time is now. With federal funding coming available, a few organizations are trying to come together to make the need known to the city.

canada.title: Early start to flu season may test Alberta hospital capacity
canada.summary: Flu season is arriving early this year, which could spell trouble for hospital capacity in the province.

canada.title: Rural schools in Alberta’s Peace region facing declining enrolment
canada.summary: The Peace River School Division is taking early steps to engage rural communities in the hopes to prevent another small school closure in northwestern Alberta. Enrolment has taken a sharp dip across their division this fall.

canada.title: Mining advocates to weigh in at court hearing on First Nation's proposed staking ban
canada.summary: The Yukon Supreme Court has granted the Yukon Chamber of Mines intervenor status at an upcoming hearing about a mineral claims staking ban sought by the First Nation Na-cho Nyäk Dun on its traditional territory.

canada.title: Carney heads to China to meet with President Xi, leaders from across Pacific Rim
canada.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney is travelling to China today, where he is set to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and leaders from across the Pacific Rim.

canada.title: N.L.’s top-billing doctor faces malpractice lawsuits from 2 former patients
canada.summary: The ophthalmologist who was Newfoundland and Labrador's top-billing doctor for the last two years straight is being sued by two former patients, including one who says his right eye was completely blinded during a botched cataract surgery.

canada.title: Extendicare says improved staff education in Manitoba will bolster care for residents with dementia
canada.summary: Extendicare, which operates 12 personal care homes in Manitoba, has set a target of certifying its entire provincial workforce in a dementia-specific care method known as the gentle persuasive approach.

canada.title: Saint John data centre would pay property tax equivalent to 8 oil refineries, study suggests
canada.summary: A report suggesting that a controversial data centre complex proposed for Saint John would eventually pay the city property taxes equivalent to eight large oil refineries has municipal officials dreaming big but wondering if it can be true.

canada.title: Moncton mulls options to prevent future flooding
canada.summary: The City of Moncton has started to consider its options for mitigating the impacts of flooding, including to a berm along the waterfront or raise Assomption Boulevard that would cost up to $15 million.

canada.title: Can Canada claw its way back into the Chinese lobster market?
canada.summary: The Canadian lobster industry is thinking of ways to recapture the Chinese market after competitors took advantage of retaliatory tariffs. Vietnam in particular was able to position its lobster well in 2025, filling the gap Canada left and becoming a strong competitor.

canada.title: Whitehorse veterinarian bringing pet care to Dawson City through a new clinic
canada.summary: Nora Vom Endt is a veterinarian based in Whitehorse. She is starting a new veterinary clinic in Dawson City next spring. Her clinic will be located in the town's downtown core and will offer similar services to clinics down South.

canada.title: St. John's, province having 'open and frank' talks on open drug use, public safety
canada.summary: The mayor of St. John's says there's been "open and frank discussions" behind the scenes with the provincial government on how to address public safety and open drug use concerns in the capital city.

canada.title: Montreal students reeling from police violence at Nov. 13 education austerity protest
canada.summary: Montreal students are denouncing the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM) for what they call unjustified acts of violence during a protest against education austerity that took place on Friday.

canada.title: Quebec to test its emergency alert system this Wednesday
canada.summary: Quebec residents can expect to hear a loud alert on Nov. 18 at 1:55 p.m., as the province tests its emergency notification system.

canada.title: Nationwide flight grounding unlikely in Canada, says aviation expert
canada.summary: An aviation management expert says Canada is less likely than the United States to ground flights nationwide as that country did on Friday afternoon, calling the Canadian system a model its southern neighbours should look to.

canada.title: One last afternoon in the park for Bailey
canada.summary: Bailey the dog was diagnosed with cancer this year, and her owners are doing everything they can to make sure she has the best time before she is gone. That included throwing her a little party at a Dartmouth park on Sunday so people could show up and give her all the attention in the world.
